title: The admin app never shows what a pack of AI credits costs, so an owner asks MettleUp for credits without knowing the price
what: The AI credits sheet only says to write to MettleUp in Help and feedback and say how many credits you want. It shows no pack and no price, although the server already sends the three packs and their rupee prices to the app, and the website notes say the prices are shown in the app when an owner needs more. The only place the prices are written is the website's About page.
expected: When an owner runs low, the sheet shows the three packs and what each costs (50 for 149 rupees, 150 for 399, 500 for 999), with the same Ask MettleUp button.
how_often: every time an owner wants more credits
fix_line: Show the three packs and their prices on the credits sheet, next to Ask MettleUp for credits

title: The server takes whatever number of credits the admin app says a task costs
what: When an owner confirms a task, the admin app works out the price itself (1 for a message or a save, 3 for a workout plan) and sends that number. The server checks only that it is between 1 and 9 and that the gym has that many; it never works it out again from the task it saved. An admin app that is old or changed in the browser could save a workout plan for 1 credit.
expected: The server works out the price from the actions saved with the task, and takes exactly that.
how_often: only with an old or altered admin app
fix_line: Let the server count the price from the saved task's actions instead of trusting the number sent

title: The AI credits sheet's price list leaves out renewals, extensions, enquiries and expenses
what: Under What uses credits the sheet lists only a message sent and a member or payment saved for 1 credit. Renewing a plan, extending a plan, saving an enquiry and saving an expense also take 1 credit each, and the website's table names enquiries and expenses.
expected: The sheet names every task that takes a credit, in the same words as the website.
how_often: every time the sheet is opened
fix_line: Change the row to name every saved task that costs 1 credit

title: Every gym gets 20 starter credits, but the website says only the free trial gets them and a monthly plan gets none
what: The server adds 20 starter credits the first time an owner opens the assistant, trial or not, so a gym already on a monthly plan also gets them. The website's table says the free trial gets 20 once and a monthly plan gets none.
expected: The website and the server agree on who gets the 20 starter credits.
fix_line: Say on the website that every gym gets 20 starter credits once, or give them only in the trial

title: Record a payment from the assistant fails for a member who owes on two plans
what: The Record a payment button under a member's dues asks to record the whole amount owed across all their plans. The draft puts that money against the oldest unpaid plan only and has no way to pick a plan, so the check refuses it: they owe less for this plan, type that or less. The owner has to lower the amount and do it a second time.
expected: Record a payment for a member with two unpaid plans either splits the money over the plans or lets the owner pick the plan, so one tap can finish.
how_often: when a member owes on more than one plan
fix_line: Prefill only the oldest plan's due, or add a plan choice to the payment card
